title: Embedded software — design & maintenance
summary: Firmware for microcontrollers, built, tested and simulated in a sealed box; long-term engagements with milestones, a warranty and monthly maintenance.
canDo: Firmware for ARM Cortex-M and RISC-V microcontrollers: bare metal, FreeRTOS, Zephyr; C, C++
Drivers from datasheets and register maps (UART, SPI, I²C, CAN, ADC, timers, DMA)
Bug fixes, porting to a new chip or SDK, security updates of libraries, CI set-up
Every delivery checked in the box: build (N1), unit tests (N2), simulation (N3), flash/RAM and static analysis (N4)
cannotDo: PCB or hardware design, choosing components, manufacturing
Signing safety certifications (ISO 26262, IEC 62304, IEC 61508, DO-178C)
Flashing devices in the field: you test on your own board (N5) and release with your own key
Code without clear ownership, or software meant to attack or break devices

fields.label: Microcontroller or board
fields.example: STM32F407VG on our own board; prototype on NUCLEO-F407

fields.label: Clock, flash and RAM available
fields.example: 168 MHz, 1 MB flash (512 KB free), 192 KB RAM (64 KB free)

fields.label: Language, RTOS/SDK and versions, toolchain, build system
fields.example: C11, FreeRTOS 10.6, STM32Cube HAL 1.27, arm-none-eabi-gcc 13, CMake

fields.label: Repository (link). Access tokens are never written here — they are sealed to the AI's box after it starts
Build command (run in the repository root)
Firmware file produced by the build (ELF, path from the repository root)
Flash limit for the firmware (bytes, optional)
RAM limit for the firmware (bytes, optional)
What must be done
fields.help: Describe the behaviour wanted, the interfaces involved and, for a bug, how to reproduce it.

fields.label: Milestones (one per line, in order: what each one delivers)
Constraints: real-time deadlines, power, coding standard, licence
Simulation: QEMU/Renode machine, if any, and the output lines that prove it works
Your test files that the AI must NOT change (one per line: path = sha256)
Hardware test you will run on your board (N5)
After delivery: monthly maintenance wanted?
optionLabels: Yes: 24 h answer, 72 h security fixes, monthly status report

acceptance: N1 build: the firmware builds from the repository with the agreed toolchain, with no new warnings; the artifact's sha256 is in the report.
N2 tests: the agreed test command passes, and every pinned test file is unchanged.
N3 simulation: where a simulation is agreed, the firmware runs in it and prints every agreed line.
N4 budgets and analysis: flash and RAM within the agreed limits; static analysis shows no new finding (only suppressions pinned in this brief count).
Delivered as a branch with a pull request, never pushed to the main branch; the AI never signs releases.
Each milestone delivers what its line in Milestones says, and nothing outside this brief.

deliverable.description: A branch and pull request in your repository, with the N1–N4 report (its hash is recorded on chain with each delivery).
